subject: Post-call: ClearBay embeddings migration and SDK/auth architecture
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Adam Cheng <adam.cheng@clearbay.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: ClearBay embeddings migration and SDK/auth architecture

Hi Adam,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and clear alignment on the goals. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

Goals you called out:
- Replace current vector store + achieve better reranking quality for short-form query matches.
- Keep inference latency <= 80ms p99 for the top-level candidate fetch and sub-second end-to-end rerank.
- Minimize migration effort from Pinecone and support a staged roll-out.

Technical notes / asks we covered:
- SDKs: you want Node + Python first; we have both production SDKs and a lightweight Go client (we'll share links).
- Auth: support for API keys today, with JWT-based service tokens and short-lived key rotation for Dedicated/Private. If you need mTLS for on-prem, we can enable.
- Routing: region-aware model routing (us-west primary, failover to us-east) and per-tenant routing policies.
- Structured output/tool calling: we can annotate embeddings and route reranker decisions with structured metadata for downstream tooling.
- Embeddings: you mentioned current vectors at 512 dims in Pinecone. Based on your recall/semantic needs we recommended testing 768 and 1536 dims options; Marissa will propose a tradeoff matrix.
- Batching & normalization: expected batch sizes today are ~50-150 per second; Redwood supports continuous batching with recommended server-side batch size ~64 for your latency SLOs. L2 (unit) normalization covers most cosine-similarity use cases — we suggested sticking to L2 and testing max-normalization if you have custom scoring.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight architecture diagram, a token/pricing example, and a migration playbook stub to help with internal planning.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with engineering (we suggest Karthik + Marissa + your eng lead) — schedule 30–45m this week.
2) Trial access / sandbox account: we'll provision sample API keys and a small trial index (50k vectors) to run migration pilots.
3) Migration plan: ingest strategy + ID mapping + roll-forward test harness (we included a playbook).

Can you confirm the team for the deep-dive and a couple of slots that work?

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

Ben —

Appreciate the summary. A few follow-ups from our side after syncing with our eng lead: 

1) Current setup: Pinecone with 512-d vectors, stored alongside metadata in our PostgreSQL. Our reranker currently reads top-1k candidates and re-scores locally.

2) Dimensionality: curious about the real-world tradeoffs you mentioned. At what point does 1536 materially improve recall for short queries vs cost/latency impact? Can Marissa share empirical numbers or a recommended sampling plan?

3) SDKs/Auth: Node + Python are critical. We also need guidance on key rotation and a workflow for short-lived credentials for our CI pipelines. Is there a hosted token service or do we self-manage?

4) Migration: we'd prefer a staged approach — dual-write into Pinecone + Redwood index for 2 weeks with a canary percentage. Does Redwood support consistent ID mapping and delta-sync? Any recommended tooling for large bulk re-ingests (500k+ vectors)?

5) Batching/latency: our production QPS is bursty (peaks ~200 qps). What batching knobs should we tune to maintain 80ms p99 for candidate fetch?

6) Normalization: confirm you recommend L2 normalization for cosine. Any gotchas with pre-normalized vectors from other providers?

If you can send the answers in a short doc and we can lock a time on the deep-dive. Thanks — we can do Tue/Wed morning PT.

—Adam
Adam Cheng
Senior SWE, ClearBay Analytics
adam.cheng@clearbay.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: ClearBay embeddings migration and SDK/auth architecture

Hi Adam —

Thanks for the clear questions. I pulled together concise answers and practical recommendations below. If helpful, we can convert this into a 1-pager for your engs.

Dimensionality tradeoffs:
- Recommendation: run a small A/B run with 768 and 1536. For short-form query recall we typically see diminishing returns after 1536 for dense transformer-based embed models, but the delta between 512->768 and 768->1536 can be significant depending on your embedding model and query types.
- Sampling plan: 5k representative queries against 50k reference vectors (we can provision) and measure recall@10/50 and reranker NDCG. Marissa will include example thresholds.

SDKs / Auth / Key rotation:
- SDKs: official SDKs available for Python and Node (npm package: @redwood/inference), Go client available as opt-in. Examples and quickstarts: https://github.com/redwood/inference-quickstarts (we'll share direct snippets in the deep-dive).
- Auth: hosted API keys for the Sandbox. For production, options: 1) short-lived JWTs issued by Redwood-managed token service (recommended for Dedicated/Hosted), 2) API keys with automated rotation via KMS for Private. We support programmatic rotation via an admin API and can drop-in with your existing secrets manager.

Routing & latency knobs / batching:
- Continuous batching: server-side continuous batching aggregates requests up to a configured target batch size and latency window. For your QPS profile we recommend: target_batch_size = 64, max_batch_latency = 12ms, max_concurrency = 48 per shard. These settings balance CPU/GPU utilization and p99 latency.
- If you see 200 qps burst, autoscale pools + burst capacity can keep p99 under 80ms; we'll provision autoscale policy during pilot.

Normalization, similarity, and pre-normalized vectors:
- We recommend L2 (unit) normalization before storage when using cosine similarity. If your existing provider stores non-normalized vectors, Redwood accepts either; we normalize at ingest (optional) and store a flag. For pre-normalized vectors, ensure consistent L2 scaling — a double-normalize will distort distances. We'll provide an ingest validator that detects normalization state and warns.

Migration strategy for Pinecone -> Redwood:
- Dual-write approach supported. Steps we recommend:
  1) Bulk export from Pinecone (or streaming via your change-capture).
  2) Re-ingest into Redwood with canonical ID mapping (we preserve your existing IDs).
  3) Run overlap sampling to verify score parity on a small set.
  4) Canary traffic split (10% at first, monitor rerank deltas and latency).
- Tooling: we provide a bulk ingestion CLI that supports parquet/ndjson uploads and a resumption token for large jobs (500k+). For very large archives we can provision parallel workers.

Practical notes on reranker + embeddings:
- Keep original metadata with vectors (tenant id, doc id, timestamp). For reranker quality, store passage-level vectors and an optional aggregated doc-level vector to speed candidate selection.

Attachments and follow-ups:
- I attached a sample architecture diagram (same as Ben), and a short migration playbook PDF. Marissa will follow up with the sampling thresholds and a quick scripts checklist.

Next steps (concrete):
1) We provision a sandbox index (50k vectors) and trial API keys (action: Ben).
2) ClearBay exports a 5k sample and we run the 768 vs 1536 experiment (action: Adam + Marissa).
3) Schedule a 45m technical deep-dive Tue/Wed morning PT — here's my availability: Tue 9–11am PT, Wed 10–12pm PT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through code samples.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
